decisions.reason: As the firm's flagship seasonal product with repeated external quality recognition and a strong fit to its core confectionery identity, its value is largely revealed and clearly worth retaining.

After two years without any visible positive signal and with several similar bread experiments already pruned, this more niche rye variant now offers limited option value relative to the cost and complexity of keeping it in the range.

The marzipan stollen remains a low-cost seasonal extension close to existing capabilities, and absent clear negative evidence it is still worth keeping as a secondary holiday option beside the flagship stollen.
